title: Spinal Cord Ischemia After Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: Pathophysiology, Detection, and Management
content: Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) is one of the most devastating complications of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair, frequently resulting in permanent neurological deficits, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality. Despite significant advances in open and endovascular aortic repair, SCI continues to pose a major clinical challenge because of its multifactorial pathophysiology, variable presentation, and narrow therapeutic window for intervention. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding the mechanisms, diagnosis, prevention, rescue management, and long-term rehabilitation of SCI following TAAA repair from a neurocritical care perspective. We review the vascular anatomy and collateral networks that underlie spinal cord perfusion and discuss established spinal cord protection strategies, including hemodynamic optimization, cerebrospinal fluid drainage, and intraoperative neuromonitoring with motor- and somatosensory-evoked potentials. Emerging diagnostic and monitoring modalities, including near-infrared spectroscopy and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, are examined for their potential role in early detection and timely intervention. We also evaluate established rescue therapies, investigational pharmacologic and neuroprotective approaches, and evolving regenerative strategies. Finally, we summarize rehabilitation principles addressing neuropathic pain, spasticity, autonomic dysfunction, mobility restoration, and psychological recovery while highlighting important gaps in the current literature and future research priorities. By integrating contemporary evidence across perioperative care and neurorehabilitation, this review provides a practical multidisciplinary framework to improve the prevention, recognition, and management of SCI after TAAA repair and to optimize long-term neurological outcomes.
